open_obligations: Note that easy-to-hard (correct labels on easy data) and weak-to-strong (noisy labels from a weaker model) are different setups.
Check whether Hase et al. tested reward modeling, where Burns et al.'s result is weakest.
Do not read either result as transferring to the other's setting.
out.other_title: Authors suggest the scalable oversight problem may be easier than previously thought
out.rationale: Hase et al. suggest from strong easy-to-hard generalization that scalable oversight may be easier than previously thought. Burns et al. report naive weak-to-strong generalization on ChatGPT reward modeling recovers only about 10% of the gap (almost never above 20%) and say their results suggest that naively using weak, human-level supervision will be insufficient to align strong, superhuman models; the two vary different axes (label difficulty versus supervisor strength).
out.scope: proposed SAME_QUESTION_DIFFERENT_SETTING: whether limited or weaker supervision is sufficient to elicit strong models' capabilities, i.e. whether scalable oversight is easier than thought

state_meaning: AI-drafted candidate; no person has reviewed it.
text: The paper reports that naive weak-to-strong generalization is poor on the ChatGPT reward modeling task: usually only roughly 10% of the performance gap is recovered, and PGR almost never exceeds 20% even for relatively small compute gaps. More generally, the authors say their results suggest that naively using weak, human-level supervision will be insufficient to align strong, superhuman models.
title: Weak-to-strong generalization is poor on ChatGPT reward modeling (about 10% PGR)
